target: route "convex-lift": the choice lift L(G), its RLT/Sherali-Adams hierarchy R_j over the choice variables, and the eight results cl:exact-lift, cl:rlt/cl:sound/cl:faces, cl:rigid, cl:collapse, cl:gap-one, cl:dw, cl:barrier, cl:cut (plus cl:union, cl:duality, cl:families in the LaTeX)
verdict: The route's central positive content survives independent reconstruction: I rebuilt Q(G), the level-j lift of cl:rlt (in the reduced coordinates of lem:transport-dim, provably equivalent), an exact rational two-phase simplex, and every named instance from the STATEMENTS in frontier.tex, and every number the route reports reproduced exactly — W_14's level-1 box ([1/2,3/5],[1/2,23/40],[15/32,11/20]) and its level-2 exactness, the dual's ([2/5,1/2],[17/40,1/2],[9/20,17/32]), DW (27 vertices, 3 Max / 3 Min / 19 non-sink average, stopping, w*(s)=1/2, R_0(s)=[1/4,3/4], R_1(s)=[9/20,11/20] computed directly on DW), the cl:gap-one certificate entry by entry, R_1={w*} on G8, S, S_r(3), H_3, H_5, R, WD(4,2,6),(6,3,7),(8,4,8), CC(1,2),(2,2),(1,4), CV(1,3),(1,4),(2,4) and G* at all seven controlled coordinates, and every Rev set. cl:exact-lift, cl:rlt, cl:sound, cl:faces, cl:rigid-pin, cl:rigid, cl:union, cl:duality, cl:gap-one, cl:dw and cl:cut's validity clause are correct as proved. But four defects survive and none is cosmetic. (1) cl:collapse's clause "the first exact level is at most min(m,k)" is FALSE — the correct consequence of its own two halves is max(m,k), and the route's own witness W_14 (m=3, k=0, min(m,k)=0) has R_0 = Q(W_14) with max x(v_1) = 1 > 1/2; the headline repeats the false clause. (2) cl:barrier is false as stated at j=0 (G8: rho_max=0 yet max_{R_0}x(5)=1>1/2) and, for j>=1, is true but NOT proved by the argument given, which yields only rho_max >= j; the JSON's extra bootstrap sentence is circular. I supply the repair: the sharper bound is j >= min(m, max(1,rho_max)), proved by pinning every rigid Max vertex at the top index and then using that h_w(x)=sum lambda_tau h_w(x^tau) with all terms >= 0 forces h_w(x^tau)=0. (3) cl:families labels three claims "theorems rather than computations" that do not follow, all traceable to (1): the one-player families at level one (cl:collapse gives only the min direction at level 0 there; WD has rho_max=2), G# at level two (I computed Rev(G#) from prop:auso-seven's printed normal form: rho_max=4, rho_min=2, so cl:collapse gives level four, and R_2(G#)={w*} is neither proved nor measured anywhere), and the b2 realisation at level one (rho_max=2, m=5, so cl:collapse gives level three; the claim happens to be true — I verified R_1={w*} at all six coordinates of B2_small_GAME.json — but it is unproved). (4) cl:rigid's class collapses into an object the paper already owns and the route does not say so: v is rigid iff the pair separator Sep(v^(0),v^(1)) <= 0 or Sep(v^(1),v^(0)) <= 0 over Q(G), which rem:own-successor explicitly licenses as a decision; so "every controlled vertex rigid" says exactly that the level-zero transport LP already names an optimal profile, and w* then follows from one linear solve — verified on G8, H_3, H_5 and R. Its advertised witness R of prop:own-stall is decided at level zero by that pair test (Rev(R) is empty), and G* likewise (all three Max vertices rigid; freezing them and taking max over Q of the Min-only game returns w* exactly, which I recomputed). So the headline "decides every stalling instance in the paper with one polynomial-size linear programme at level one" is true but is not evidence of anything the paper's level-zero machinery did not already do; the genuinely new content is cl:gap-one and cl:dw. Verdict: the route is not sound as written; with the min(m,k) clause deleted, cl:barrier restricted to j>=1 and reproved, cl:families' three theorem claims demoted to measurements (two of them to open), and the pair-test collapse of cl:rigid stated, what remains is correct.

findings.result_name: cl:collapse — the level at which the hierarchy collapses
findings.defect: The final clause of the theorem, "so the first exact level is at most min(m,k)", is false; the correct consequence of the theorem's own two halves is max(m,k). Since max(min(k,rho_min+1), min(m,rho_max+1)) <= max(k,m) and is in general larger than min(m,k), the clause does not follow, and it is refuted by the route's own witness. The headline repeats it ("collapses at level min(|Vmax|,|Vmin|)") and cl:families builds three claims on it (see the separate finding).
findings.evidence: W_14 (thm:lasserre-vacuous) has m=3, k=0, so min(m,k)=0, and R_0 = Q(G) by cl:sound. Rebuilt from the paper's definition (12 non-sink vertices, stopping by lem:trapchar, w*=(1/2,1/2,15/32), reduced rows u1>=u2, u1>=u3, u2>=1/2, u2>=(7/8)u1, u3>=15/32, u3>=(7/8)u1), my exact simplex gives max_{R_0} x(v_1) = 1 > 1/2 = w*(v_1); the route itself reports the same number ("on W_14 level 0 gives max x(v_1)=1") and measures the first exact level as 2. The two halves of the theorem are correct as proved: I checked the splitting/normalisation/freezing argument line by line, including that a trap of the frozen game is a trap of G and that x^tau agrees with the sink payoffs. Code: /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/r17-audit-convex-lift-correctness/{simplex.py,red.py,inst.py,lift.py}; log logs_w14_j2.txt.

findings.result_name: cl:barrier — what an instance defeating the hierarchy must contain
findings.defect: False as stated at j=0, and unproved for j>=1. From max_{R_j}x(v) > w*(v) and cl:collapse one gets j < min(m, rho_max+1), i.e. m > j and rho_max >= j — never rho_max > j. The LaTeX proof is the single line "cl:collapse and cl:sound", which cannot yield the stated "more than j reversing Max vertices"; the JSON's supplementary sentence ("since rho_max is an integer with rho_max >= j it is in fact > j once the same argument is applied to the exact bound min(m,rho_max+1) > j") is circular. The corollary is used to size the next construction ("at least three reversing Max and three reversing Min vertices, so the smallest candidate has |C| = 6").
findings.evidence: Refutation at j=0: G8 of prop:simorder-stalls has one Max vertex with A_v identically -1/10 on Q(G8), so rho_max = 0, while max_{R_0} x(5) = 1 > 1/2 = w*(5) (my exact LP; R_0 box on G8 = [1/2,1]). H_3 (A_v = +1/16), H_5 (+1/64) and R of prop:own-stall (Rev empty, R_0 box at the Max vertex 4 = [0,1] with w*(4)=1/2) refute it identically. Repair, which I verified: for j>=1 and rho_max <= j the max direction IS exact, by (i) splitting x at each rigid Max w from the top index, so x(w)=max_i x(w^(i)) by cl:rigid-pin, i.e. h_w(x)=0 for the linear form h_w(y)=y(w)-y(w^(a_w)); (ii) splitting on S=Rev∩Vmax; (iii) h_w(x)=sum_tau lambda_tau h_w(x^tau) with every h_w(x^tau) >= 0 on Q, forcing h_w(x^tau)=0; (iv) hence x^tau <= T_{sigma_tau} x^tau, so x^tau <= val_{sigma_tau} <= w*. This gives the sharper bound j >= min(m, max(1,rho_max)) (strictly better than min(m,rho_max+1) whenever 1 <= rho_max < m: the b2 realisation has rho_max=2, m=5, sharp bound 2 versus the route's 3), and from it "more than j reversing" does follow for j>=1 — but by an argument the route does not give.

findings.result_name: cl:families / cl:barrier verification — three claims presented as theorems do not follow
findings.defect: cl:families says "Three of these are theorems rather than computations" and then asserts (a) "WD, CC, S, S_r and every one-player family have min(m,k)=0, so cl:collapse applies"; (b) "G^sharp ((m,k)=(4,2)) satisfies R_2={w*} ... by cl:collapse alone"; (c) "the level-two realisation of prop:b2-realised ((m,k)=(5,1)) satisfies R_1={w*}, by cl:collapse alone". None follows: for a one-player Max game cl:collapse gives only the MIN direction at level 0; the MAX direction needs j >= min(m,rho_max+1). cl:barrier's verification field repeats it ("R_1={w*} was proved (not merely measured) on the one-player families, on R, and on the b2 realisation, and R_2={w*} on G-sharp"); of those only the R row is genuinely proved (Rev(R) empty, cl:rigid).
findings.evidence: Rev computed exactly over Q(G) by 2|C| LPs: WD(4,2,6) both Max vertices reversing (A_v range [-7/512, 23/128]), so cl:collapse's max half needs level min(2,3)=2, not 1; same for CC (both reversing) and CV (all three reversing). G#: I rebuilt its reduced system from the harmonic normal form printed in prop:auso-seven (twelve rows over 1/128) and got w*=(6355898/11387053, 129936/186673, 130048/186673, 131072/186673, 64/115, 1031367/1493384) with ALL SIX controlled vertices reversing, rho_max=4, rho_min=2; cl:collapse therefore gives level 4, and the sharper bound min(m,max(1,rho_max))=4 as well, so R_2(G#)={w*} is neither proved nor measured — it is an open assertion inside a "proved" proposition. b2: from /data/ssg-proof/scripts/blowup/B2_small_GAME.json (136 non-sink, 5 Max, 1 Min, stopping) I computed rho_max=2, rho_min=0, so cl:collapse gives level 3 for the max half; the claim is nevertheless TRUE — my exact LP returns R_1 = {w*} at all six controlled coordinates (w*(c_0)=28855283296/52702783249, ..., w*(c_5)=53201928577/105405566498) — but unproved. The one-player level-1 claims are also true as measurements: I reproduced R_1={w*} on WD(4,2,6),(6,3,7),(8,4,8), CC(1,2),(2,2),(1,4), CV(1,3),(1,4),(2,4), S, S_r(3). Logs: logs_b2.txt, logs_cvcc.txt, gsharp.py.

findings.result_name: cl:rigid — rigid games are one linear programme
findings.defect: The theorem is true, but its hypothesis collapses into an object the paper already owns and the route does not say so (round rule 0). v is rigid, i.e. A_v(x)=x(v^(0))-x(v^(1)) has constant weak sign on Q(G), if and only if min A_v >= 0 or max A_v <= 0, i.e. if and only if Sep(v^(1),v^(0)) <= 0 or Sep(v^(0),v^(1)) <= 0 — exactly the non-strict PAIR test of def:transport that rem:own-successor explicitly licenses as a decision ("note that (i) is non-strict, and so is the pair test's Sep(v^(0),v^(1)) <= 0; both decide"). So "every controlled vertex is rigid" says precisely that the level-zero transport LP already names an optimal profile sigma*, and then w* = val_{sigma*} by one linear solve (T_{sigma*}w* = Tw* = w*, uniqueness by thm:contraction) — no lift and no level-one LP. cl:rigid's why_not_implied compounds this by advertising R of prop:own-stall as an instance the paper's mechanism cannot decide; prop:own-stall is about the OWN-SUCCESSOR separators Sep(v,v^(i)), and Rev(R) being empty is literally the statement that the pair test decides all five of its controlled vertices.
findings.evidence: Equivalence is immediate from Sep(p,q)=max{x(q)-x(p)} over Q(G). Verified computationally: on G8, H_3, H_5 and R the sign of A_v over Q names a profile whose exact profile value equals w* on the nose (profile_value vs wstar_brute, both exact: G8 {5:1}, H_3 {7:0}, H_5 {11:0}, R {0:1,1:0,4:0,6:1,7:1}). The collapse extends to the rest of cl:families' list: G* has Rev(G*) = {3,5,6} ⊆ Vmin, so the pair test decides all three Max vertices; freezing them to the pair-test actions {0:1,1:1,2:1} leaves a stopping Min-only game on which max over Q returns exactly w* at every Min vertex (27/62, 35/62, 24/31, 19/31). The one-player families are level-0 exact by thm:one-player, which the route itself lists as a restatement. Side observation for the paper: rem:own-stall's "the transport certificate alone, even read in the strongest way ... is not a decision rule" is inaccurate for R, since the pair reading of def:transport does decide it.

findings.result_name: cl:exact-lift — the choice lift is exact and already convex
findings.defect: Part (b) states L(G) = {w*} x conv(Opt) "where Opt is the optimal subcube of thm:opt-subcube", but the route's choice variables range over C = Vmax u Vmin, whereas thm:opt-subcube is stated only for {0,1}^{Vmax} ("Opt := {sigma : val_sigma = w*}", "a nonempty subcube of {0,1}^{Vmax}"). The object needed is the product of the Max optimal subcube with its Min dual, which the paper does not state (it is immediate from lem:duality). The route's displayed argument re-derives the pinning from the bilinear row, so only the citation overreaches.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.3340-3392: thm:opt-subcube's statement and proof are entirely about v in Vmax.

findings.result_name: cl:dw — the level-one relaxation does not decide the threshold
findings.defect: The LaTeX proof says level-two exactness on DW "was also computed directly on DW in exact rational arithmetic", while the route's own verification field says that direct level-two computation was done in float ("level 2 at s returns 1/2 on both sides (float, and exactly via cl:union ...)"). The claim itself is fine — it follows from cl:union together with level-two exactness of the two halves — but the LaTeX asserts an exact computation that was not performed.
findings.evidence: Route JSON, cl:dw verification. I confirmed the substance independently: R_2(W_14) = {w*} exactly (all six bounds: 1/2, 1/2, 15/32) and R_2(W_14bar) = {w*} exactly, and cl:union's proof (restriction one way, product the other) is correct, so R_2(DW)={w*}. Log logs_w14_j2.txt.

findings.defect: The verification asserts that "the level-|C| relaxation returns exactly w*" on all 19 instances while the same field says the check was not a fresh computation. For DW that is a level-6 lift with 3^6 = 729 index blocks; the statement is a consequence of cl:collapse, not a measurement, and should be labelled as such.
findings.evidence: Route JSON, cl:exact-lift verification: "Verified as a consequence of results already machine-checked in the harness rather than by fresh computation", immediately followed by the claim that the level-|C| relaxation was run on all 19.

findings.defect: The LaTeX statement adds a clause absent from the JSON and absent from the proof: the cuts "cut Q(G) strictly whenever some vertex is value-distinguishing with both faces nonempty". The proof establishes validity only, and the clause needs a hypothesis: the convention M_{v,i}=0 read as 0 can make the cut vacuous.
findings.evidence: Since each h_i has constant sign on Q(G), the cut's left-hand side is affine there, so max over Q is one LP. I ran it: the max is 2 (strict cut) at every controlled vertex of S, S_r(3), G8, H_3, W_14 and WD(4,2,6), and at four of the five controlled vertices of R — but at vertex 6 of R, M_{6,1} = 0 and the max is exactly 1, so the cut is vacuous there.

findings.defect: The cut is derived FROM membership in R_1, so it can never be stronger than R_1; its advertised non-vacuity is demonstrated on S, where R_1 is already the single point w*.
findings.evidence: On S of prop:transport-stalls the reduced readouts are x(a)=1/2 and x(b)=t/2+1/8 (recomputed), so M_0=1/2, M_1=3/8 and the cut reads t <= 7/10, trimming Q(S)=[1/2,1] — while my exact LP gives R_1(S) = {1/2} = {w*} (also forced by cl:collapse, m=1). F_v^1 = {t=1/4} is empty in Q(S), so the cut's decomposition x = lambda pi + (1-lambda) kappa degenerates there; the bound still holds but the proof as written presumes both points exist.

findings.result_name: cl:exact-lift — the choice lift is exact and already convex
findings.defect: Part (a) is a two-line extension of the computation already inside the proof of thm:transport-objective, which shows that x in Q(G) with obj_sigma(x)=0 satisfies Tx=x and hence x=w*; the fractional-y case adds only that a convex combination of two numbers is at most their maximum. The why_not_implied ("in them the branching disappears entirely") overstates the distance, though the statement itself is not literally implied.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.14014-14052, proof of thm:transport-objective: "Suppose x in Q(G) has obj_sigma(x)=0. Every term is nonnegative, so x(v)=x(v^(sigma(v))) ... Hence Tx=x, so x=w* by thm:contraction."

findings.result_name: cl:dw — the level-one relaxation does not decide the threshold
findings.defect: The threshold demonstration is at w*(s) = 1/2 exactly, the boundary case: any relaxation with a nonzero gap at s fails to decide val(s) >= 1/2 there. The route does not exhibit an instance whose value differs from 1/2 and whose level-one interval still straddles 1/2 (the interval [9/20,11/20] has width 1/10 and is centred at w*(s), so such a perturbation is plausible but is not shown).
findings.evidence: My independent build of DW: w*(s) = 1/2 by brute force over all 2^3 x 2^3 positional pairs; R_1 at s = [9/20, 11/20] by exact LP directly on DW (not through cl:union), 195 s.

findings.defect: Reproduction record: every number the route reports and that I recomputed from the statements reproduced exactly, in independent code (my own exact two-phase simplex, my own reduced-form/lift builder). No instance of the project's standing errors was found in the route's computations: values are taken by brute force over positional pairs or by exact linear solves (no greedy policy iteration), rows are accumulated rather than built as dict literals, DW's fresh root does not collide with the sinks (n=25, t0=25, t1=26, verified stopping by the trap test), sinks are pinned, and no fifth theorem is imported (LP polynomiality is already used throughout frontier.tex, e.g. def:transport and thm:eval-stopfree).
findings.evidence: Reproduced: R_0/R_1 on G8 ([1/2,1] -> {1/2}), H_3 ({9/16}), H_5 ({33/64}), R ({1/2,1/2,1/2,0,1/2} from R_0 boxes that include [0,1] at vertex 4), S, S_r(3), WD(4,2,6),(6,3,7),(8,4,8), CC(1,2),(2,2),(1,4), CV(1,3),(1,4),(2,4) (N = 6e+s+5 checked against prop:cv-values), G* (R_0 at v_0 = [3/5,1]; R_1 = {w*} at all seven: 24/31, 43/62, 49/62, 27/62, 35/62, 24/31, 19/31), W_14 (R_0 max x(v_1)=1; R_1 box; R_2={w*}), W_14bar (R_1 box; R_2={w*}), DW, and the cl:gap-one certificate (all five points in Q, all six tightness flags, both convex identities, 3/5 > 1/2).
